To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

elite female volleyball players are better than semi professional players in dynamic balance performance and that volleyball players have a better dynamic balance performance than athletes of other sport.

1) elite athletes performed significantly better than semi professional players; 2 ) there were no significant differences between the four positions; 3) there were significant differences in dynamic balance characteristics between female volleyball players and NCAA Division I female players practicing six different sports.
Elite female volleyball players scored significantly higher on dynamic posturality control tasks than semi professional volleyball players.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the balance of volleyball players.

the development and evaluation of new methods for the analysis of the Star Excursion Balance test (SEBT) and the comparison of dynamic balance characteristics between volleyball players and athletes of different sports.
the study of the relationship between balance and sport specific characteristics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dynamic postural control performance of elite athletes is superior to that of semi-professional players and is sport-specific.
the EG scored higher on the SEBT than the SG, and that the EG had better dynamic postural control than the NCAA Division 1 female athletes practicing other sports.
dynamic balance characteristics are sport specific, and that the sport-specific differences in dynamic posturography performance are related to the specific demands of the sport.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SEBT can be used to assess dynamic postural control in female volleyball players, but that it is not a sport specific measure.

the SEBT can be used as an assessment tool in female volleyball players to identify differences in dynamic balance performance between competition levels and positions, as well as to compare dynamic balance between female professional volleyball players and NCAA Division I female players practicing six different sports.
the SEBT is a valid tool for evaluating dynamic postural control in female volleyball players.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SEBT performance can be used as an indicator of sport specific dynamic postural control and that the SEBT may be useful in identifying athletes at risk of developing non-contact ACL injuries.

the sport-specific differences are not limited to a single sport, but extend to a variety of sports, and that the SEBT is not only a sport-specific but also a competition level specific tool for the assessment of dynamic postural control.
dynamic postural control is a sport specific skill.
